summary.text: A 47-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease of unknown histological etiology had been on peritoneal dialysis for six months before a kidney transplant from a donation after brain death donor. Her history included chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, diverticulosis of the sigmoid colon and allergic asthma. She received basiliximab and methylprednisolone induction, then tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil and methylprednisolone, and her postoperative course was uneventful.

One month after transplantation she was treated with meropenem for a multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa urinary tract infection. She also developed acute angle-closure glaucoma, managed with diuretics and laser peripheral iridotomy, and erosive gastritis with CMV reactivation treated with valganciclovir. Three months after transplantation a fall in the field caused a minor left knee laceration that she self-treated.

One week later, on day 7, examination showed a nodule with raised red edges and a central ulcerated area, concurrent with severe neutropenia. She was hospitalized for suspected invasive fungal infection, with biopsy and cutaneous swab, and a total-body TC scan confirmed no systemic involvement. Histology, stains, culture and ITS sequencing confirmed cutaneous alternariosis due to Alternaria infectoria; serum β-D-glucan was not performed.

Voriconazole was started while awaiting microbiological diagnosis and was switched to isavuconazole after visual hallucinations began, continued for eight weeks. Complete surgical excision with systemic antifungal therapy led to resolution, and abdominal ultrasound excluded visceral nodular involvement. To date she remains in good health with excellent graft function, serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dL, and no recurrence of alternariosis.
